TeleAbsence research assets — retrieved 2026-10-02
Primary source: Ishii et al., TeleAbsence: A Vision of Past and Afterlife Telepresence, PRESENCE 34 (2025), 65–95. DOI 10.1162/PRES_a_00441
MIT-hosted PDF: https://trackr-media.tangiblemedia.org/publishedmedia/Papers/731-MTA3N/Published/PDF
MIT summary: https://www.media.mit.edu/articles/teleabsence-poetic-encounters-with-the-past/

Original embedded JPEGs extracted without recompression:
assets/p10-0.jpeg — Figure 2, Presence of Absence: Hiroshima stone steps. Credits in paper: U.S. armed forces / unknown photographer, public domain; Matsushige Yoshito, public domain. No claim about the identity of the shadow is made in this board.
assets/p12-0.jpeg — Figure 3, Illusory Communication: Wind Phone. Credits in paper: Matthew Komatsu, CC BY-SA 4.0; Kahoku Shimpō (paper text transliteration), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Original composite preserved.
assets/p14-0.jpeg — Figure 4, Materiality of Memory: Impact Steel. Beyond My Ken, CC BY-SA 4.0.
assets/p15-0.jpeg — Figure 5, Traces of Reflection: Kenji Miyazawa manuscript, courtesy Miyazawa Kenji Memorial Museum. The source has inconsistent dates; the board intentionally omits the date.
assets/p17-0.jpeg — Figure 6, Remote Time: Notre-Dame interior before the fire. Dennis G. Jarvis, CC BY-SA 4.0. The photo shows the space, not the acoustic simulation apparatus.

The five historical/cultural cases are examples cited by the MIT paper, not five products developed by MIT.
Spectral Fluid design transfer, proposed extensions and evaluation questions are original project analysis, not MIT claims or verified user-study results.
Original assets and credits are provided for traceability. The generated board is a visual layout preview; retain these source photographs when implementing the final coded webpage.
